system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent PhaseBio Pharmaceuticals Inc. (PB); counterparty is SFJ Pharmaceuticals X, Ltd. (SFJ).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Rule and exact checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Finding rationale:
PB has no usable convenience exit. 14.2.2 is gated on SFJ having paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs, closes on receipt of the first Regulatory Approval, carries a redacted notice period, and conditions the exit on paying SFJ 300% of Development Costs, so over a Term running to the last Approval Payment (14.1) PB cannot leave on notice at the preferred (30 days) or fallback (60-90 days) standard. That fails the fallback on material terms. The redline cures the preferred checklist in operative language: 14.2.2's gating sentence and the 300% exit payment sentence are replaced by "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ, in which case SFJ will refund to PB, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by PB to SFJ under this Agreement, if any, for the period after the effective date of termination"; the now-orphaned "reduced by the amount previously paid by PB to SFJ pursuant to this Section 14.2.2" credit is conformed; and new 14.2.11 bars SFJ convenience termination during the Term. Section 11.1.1.4 continues to govern the Trial Data Package transfer and its consideration. SFJ's event-triggered exits (14.2.3, 14.2.6, 14.2.10) and their payment formulas are untouched and consistent with 14.2.11, and the Section 5.2.2.2 cross-reference to 14.2.10 remains intact.

Parties: we represent PhaseBio Pharmaceuticals Inc. (PB); counterparty is SFJ Pharmaceuticals X, Ltd. (SFJ).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

- **What the document says:** SFJ's only representation/warranty is the funding covenant at 13.5 (p0739). All other warranty content in Article 13 is PB-side (13.1–13.4), and 13.6.2 disclaims everything "EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13" (p0743). - **Why actionable:** No conformance warranty for the SFJ Services plus a sweeping disclaimer sits at walk-away, not fallback.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** new 13.5.1 in Article 13 — 30-day conformance warranty for the SFJ Services with re-performance/repair/replacement or refund at PB's election; placed inside Article 13 so the 13.6.2 carve-out preserves it.

- No minimality or intent defect arises because no text was changed, deleted or duplicated; the failure is one of completeness, not of scope.
- Severity retained at medium: the clause sits at walk-away (sweeping 13.6.2 disclaimer with no conformance warranty), but the target obligation here is oversight/funding rather than software supply, so no escalation is warranted.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent PhaseBio Pharmaceuticals Inc. (PB); counterparty is SFJ Pharmaceuticals X, Ltd. (SFJ).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Rule and exact checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",

elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: New Section 14.2.11 does not eliminate PB-payable liquidated amounts; it expressly characterises the Development Cost-based termination payments as "a liquidated amount" and converts them into "a single early-termination fee" capped at three times average monthly Development Costs. A capped liquidated fee remains a Customer-payable liquidated amount, and the retained 14.2.1-14.2.10 payment formulas are superseded rather than deleted, so the preferred no-LD outcome is not achieved.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: 14.2.11 sweeps in "each amount payable by PB under Sections 14.2.1 through 14.2.10 that is calculated by reference to Development Costs (including interest thereon and any such amount expressed as consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package)", deems each a liquidated amount, and provides it "is payable solely as a single early-termination fee". The purchase-price framing of the Trial Data Package and the 25% interest in 14.2.10 are expressly captured, so no Development Cost-based liquidated amount escapes the recharacterisation; Approval Payments/Buy-Out Payments are commercial consideration under ARTICLE 6, not liquidated amounts.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The fee is "not exceeding three (3) times the average monthly Development Costs paid or incurred during the twelve (12) months preceding the effective date of termination" - a three-month multiple of the only recurring monetary run-rate in this funding agreement (PB pays no recurring subscription/service fee; Development Costs, which include the SFJ Interim Management Fee and PB Costs, are the run-rate analogue). The multiple is three, computed on a trailing twelve-month average, so the cap is computable and does not exceed the three-month threshold.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Closing words: "which fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by PB under this Agreement", reinforced by "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement" and by the express statement that the 14.2.1-14.2.10 amounts are "superseded by this Section 14.2.11". The exclusivity statement is Agreement-wide, not limited to Article 14.

reasons: Fallback is complete: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (single early-termination fee, three-month cap, sole liquidated amount), so the redline is position-complete at the fallback level. Preferred is not met and should be offered as the opening ask - the clean preferred fix is to delete the Development Cost multiples in 14.2.1, 14.2.2, 14.2.5.2, 14.2.6, 14.2.7, 14.2.8.1, 14.2.9 and 14.2.10 outright rather than cap them.

Minimality holds: the change is a single concise insertion (14.2.11) with no deletions elsewhere, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural boilerplate, and no new requirement outside the LD checklist. The 'notwithstanding' override is narrower in practice than surgically rewriting eight retained subsections, and scoping it to Development Cost-based amounts is what preserves the ARTICLE 6 Approval Payments, Buy-Out Payment and Section 6.2 adjustment mechanics verbatim. The parenthetical on interest and Trial Data Package consideration is necessary to stop 14.2.10 and the purchase-price framing escaping the cap, so it is not an extra.

Intent is preserved: the retained 300%/150%/100% and cost-plus-25% sentences are expressly superseded rather than left in silent conflict, Section 6.4 default interest, the mutual right to pursue unliquidated damages at law, and all termination triggers/notice periods survive unchanged; no cross-reference is left dangling and no term is left undefined ('Development Costs' and 'Trial Data Package' are both defined).

Base-substitution caution to flag in the cover note (not a defect requiring repair): the cap is measured against Development Costs incurred by SFJ rather than 'fees' paid by PB, because this Agreement contains no recurring Customer-paid fee. If SFJ pushes back, be ready to fix the base to a stated dollar figure equal to three months of the then-current Development Cost budget to avoid argument about which costs enter the average.

Optional hardening: for a termination occurring within the first twelve months, the twelve-month lookback averages in pre-Effective Date months of zero cost (a result favourable to PB but likely to be challenged). Consider 'the twelve (12) months (or, if shorter, the period since the Effective Date) preceding the effective date of termination' only if SFJ raises it - adding it unprompted is unnecessary.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rewritten 14.2.2: "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ". The gating conditions (SFJ having paid/incurred $60 million of Development Costs; pre-first-Regulatory-Approval window) are deleted, so the election is unconditional. There are no Order Forms in this co-development structure, so "the Agreement" is the full covered scope. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a naming artefact — our party is styled "PB", not one of the generic Customer aliases — and is contradicted by the operative text.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ" replaces the redacted [***] notice period; 30 days is at (not above) the preferred ceiling and the notice is expressly written.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case SFJ will refund to PB, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by PB to SFJ under this Agreement, if any, for the period after the effective date of termination." The words "pro rata" are express (not merely inferred from a post-termination period), the payer is the counterparty, and the trigger is PB's convenience termination. The 300% Development Cost exit payment that would have negated any net refund is deleted.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: New 14.2.11: "SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term." Term is defined at 1.1.185/14.1, so the trigger is not undefined. Retained SFJ exits are event-conditioned, not convenience: 14.2.6 requires a Change of Control of PB and 14.2.10 requires a JSC/Executive-Officer deadlock under Section 5.2.4; "in its sole discretion" in each is discretion to invoke a triggered right, not an at-will right, so neither contradicts 14.2.11.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered notice period is thirty (30) days, which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (it is more favourable to us, but the fallback element is not literally satisfied). Immaterial here because the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the redline deletes the 300% Development Costs exit payment and adds no substitute fee, so no early-termination fee survives in 14.2.2 to be capped. The retained Approval Payment sentence is contingent on PB electing to continue development and actually obtaining Regulatory Approval, not an exit charge.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: 14.2.11 removes any SFJ convenience right during the Term entirely, which is stronger than confining it to term end; the surviving SFJ rights (14.2.3, 14.2.6, 14.2.10) are event-triggered.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no SFJ convenience right under 14.2.11, there is no convenience notice period to set.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete in operative language: unconditional PB election, 30 days' written notice, express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts, and an express bar on SFJ convenience termination during the Term.

The failing regex "Customer convenience termination present" is a party-alias artefact (our party is "PB"); substantively the operative sentence grants the convenience right, so the mechanical failure does not defeat coverage.

Edits stay inside the checklist: only the gating sentence, the redacted notice period and the 300% exit payment are removed. Removing the 300% penalty is necessary, not surplus, because a mandatory exit payment of 300% of Development Costs would contradict the pro-rata-refund element and the rule's "leave on notice without penalty" standard.

Deleting the trailing credit "and reduced by the amount previously paid by PB to SFJ pursuant to this Section 14.2.2" is a conforming change that avoids a dangling reference to a payment that no longer exists; it is not cosmetic surplus.

Favourable and unrelated language survives: the ARTICLE 6 Approval Payment continuation, the Section 6.2 adjustment and Section 6.7 Buy-Out carve-out remain in 14.2.2; 14.2.6, 14.2.10 and their payment formulas and the Section 5.2.2.2 cross-reference to 14.2.10 are untouched and are consistent with 14.2.11.

Diligence point (verify, does not currently defeat the finding): the deleted sentence framed the 300% payment as consideration "in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package ... as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4". Confirm Section 11.1.1.4 does not itself cross-refer to a payment "pursuant to Section 14.2.2"; if it does, conform that reference or add a short clause stating that on a 14.2.2 termination the Trial Data Package transfer is governed by, and consideration determined under, Section 11.1.1.4, to avoid a dangling cross-reference.

Optional tightening if SFJ pushes back on the deleted consideration: rather than reinstating a percentage exit payment, fall back to the playbook cap (60–90 days' notice with an early-termination fee not exceeding three months' fees) as already offered in the margin comment.

system.text:
You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-a684a158","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"INDEMNIFICATION AND INSURANCE","rationale":"Article 12 contains mutual indemnities, but SFJ's indemnity (12.1.1(a)-(f)) is confined to its gross negligence/wilful misconduct, breaches of the Agreement, Protocol and AZ License and post-Program-Transfer trial and product liability; it says nothing about third-party intellectual-property infringement. Conversely, PB's indemnity at 12.1.2(f) covers infringement claims caused by \"either Party\" in performing its duties, so PB carries a one-way IP indemnity that also protects SFJ for SFJ's own conduct. That fails the fallback (no Vendor IP indemnity) and sits at the walk-away line. We add a reciprocal SFJ IP indemnity at the fallback level with the customary modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies, and a super-cap of three times the aggregate amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under the Agreement in the preceding twelve months (floored at three times the first twelve months' amounts so the cap cannot be zero before Approval Payments fall due, and scoped to the new indemnity so SFJ's existing uncapped indemnities are unaffected). We also narrow 12.1.2(f) to PB's own performance to remove the circularity and conform the 12.2.1 cross-reference so the existing notice, control-of-defence and cooperation mechanics apply to the new indemnity.","proposal":"Add SFJ third-party IP indemnity (standard exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, 3x annual amounts super-cap with a non-zero floor) and conform PB's IP indemnity and the procedure cross-reference.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-ip-ad97f257","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION","rationale":"Article 11 is otherwise favourable: PB is the sole owner of, and SFJ assigns, all Trial Inventions (p0659), and each Party retains its pre-Effective Date IP (p0650), so the fallback deliverable elements are exceeded by outright PB ownership and there is no joint ownership anywhere. The failure is Section 11.1.1.4: SFJ is made sole and exclusive owner of the Trial Data Package, i.e. all clinical trial data and Research Results generated under our Development Program, until PB buys it back (Article 6 pricing at p0489; termination buy-backs at p0750 et seq.). Vesting our own data in the counterparty is walk-away territory and gives SFJ rights far beyond processing to perform the services. The redline flips ownership to PB, limits SFJ to processing the data solely to perform its obligations, and conforms the retained sale wording so the Exhibit K agreement confirms PB's ownership; the payment consideration and the 14.3.1 backstop assignment (p0783) are left intact.","proposal":"PB owns the Trial Data Package and Research Results from the outset; SFJ may process them only to perform its obligations, with the Exhibit K mechanic conformed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-adbfb2f5","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 15.3.2 If to SFJ:","rationale":"Section 15.6 already gives PB the preferred affiliate and successor carve-outs, but the bargain fails the rule on three points. Section 14.2.6 lets SFJ terminate in its sole discretion on a Change of Control of PB (with a 150% Development Costs payment) — expressly walk-away territory. The no-consent carve-out is mutual, so SFJ may assign to its Affiliates or a successor without our consent, and no reasonableness standard governs consent for other assignments. The competitor bar lapses at Program Transfer. We target preferred: PB keeps its carve-outs, SFJ assignments need our consent (not unreasonably withheld), the competitor bar is permanent, and SFJ's change-of-control termination right is removed together with the consequences expressly conditioned on that termination. Article 6 (including the Section 6.2 adjustment and Section 6.7 buy-out credit) continues to govern Approval Payments, and no other provision cross-refers to Section 14.2.6.","proposal":"PB-only no-consent assignment carve-out, reasonableness standard for SFJ assignments, permanent competitor-assignment bar, and removal of SFJ's Change of Control termination right and its dependent consequences.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-68496efd","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 3.9 IDMC","rationale":"The only exclusivity covenant in the Agreement is Section 3.19, which binds SFJ (and its Affiliates) not to trial or sell Competing Products during the Exclusive Period (ending November 21, 2022 / November 21, 2024 per Section 1.1.68). That restriction runs in PB's favour and, per the detection guidance, exclusivity granted to Customer is acceptable and is not flagged. We found no reciprocal covenant requiring PB to source, purchase or procure exclusively from SFJ, no \"sole supplier\" language, and no bar on PB engaging third parties for supply — indeed PB is itself the GMP Manufacturer and supplier of Product under Section 3.14.1. The Section 7.5 negative covenants (indebtedness, liens, distributions and the Section 7.5.5 consent right over non-Excluded Licensing Transactions) are financing-style restrictions tied to SFJ's security interest and an out-licensing consent mechanic; they are not a sourcing or sole-supplier obligation and fall outside this rule's boundary (they are noted here only for completeness). The clause set therefore meets the preferred position — PB carries no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation — so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-f8077e37","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"Article 14.2 imposes fixed, formula-driven termination payments on PB (our party): 300% of Development Costs where SFJ terminates for PB's material breach (14.2.1), on PB's at-will termination (14.2.2), on bankruptcy termination (14.2.5.2) and on safety terminations attributable to PB (14.2.7); 150% on Change of Control (14.2.6) and compliance breach (14.2.8.1); 100% on Adverse Patent Impact (14.2.9); and Development Costs plus 25% annual interest on a JSC-decision termination (14.2.10). These are liquidated amounts payable by Customer and the breach-triggered multiples are punitive, so both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single capped early-termination fee) fail. Fixing the earlier draft's gaps, the revised Section 14.2.11 (i) deems every Development Cost-based amount a liquidated amount \"however expressed as consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package\", so the purchase-price framing cannot escape the cap; (ii) makes the cap computable as three (3) times average monthly Development Costs over the twelve months preceding termination, the only recurring cost run-rate in the Agreement; and (iii) expressly supersedes the retained 14.2.1-14.2.10 formulas and states the fee is the sole liquidated amount, removing the internal inconsistency. The override is scoped to Development Cost-based amounts so the Article 6 Approval Payments, Buy-Out Payments and all other commercial terms in those subsections are preserved verbatim. We leave 14.2.1's mutual right to pursue unliquidated damages at law intact: it is not a liquidated amount, sits outside this checklist, and also benefits PB as non-breaching party. Section 6.4 late-payment interest is ordinary default interest and is not flagged.","proposal":"Deem every Development Cost-based termination payment by PB to be superseded by a single early-termination fee capped at three times average monthly Development Costs.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-license-94275aab","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION","rationale":"There is no conventional vendor-to-customer licence grant here: PB is the sole and exclusive owner of all Trial Inventions (11.1.1.3(a)) and acquires sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package (11.1.1.4), which is stronger than any licence. The only rights that reach PB as a licence are the flow-down licences SFJ must procure from its consultants and Third Party contractors under 11.1.1.3(b)-(c), and those are expressly \"worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable ... with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers\". Measured against the fallback checklist: PB's Affiliates are covered without even a written-notice mechanic, because PB may sublicense through multiple tiers and may freely assign; and the licence is transferable to a successor, both by its own \"freely-assignable\" terms and by Section 15.6, which lets either Party assign this Agreement and all rights to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger, sale of stock or sale of assets without consent. Nothing is revocable at SFJ's discretion, and no clause excludes affiliates or contractors. This sits at (and in respect of affiliate/sublicence coverage above) the fallback position, so we do not redline it. Two preferred-only refinements are noted but not flagged: the fully-paid licences are not expressly labelled \"perpetual\" or \"irrevocable\", and SFJ's obligation to procure them is a commercially reasonable efforts obligation (11.1.1.3(c)/p0662). Neither is a material failure of the fallback, and PB's outright ownership of Trial Inventions makes the residual licence path a secondary safety net.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-9b2244a9","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 3.9 IDMC","rationale":"The only exclusivity/non-compete covenant in the Agreement (Section 3.19, with the \"Exclusive Period\" and \"Competing Product\"/\"Brilinta Competing Product\" definitions at 1.1.68, 1.1.43 and 1.1.18) binds SFJ and its Affiliates, not PB; it restrains the counterparty and therefore benefits us. No provision restricts the businesses PB may operate or the products it may develop, acquire or sell, and Section 15.15 confirms all rights not expressly granted to SFJ are reserved to PB and its Affiliates. The remaining PB-side negative covenants in Article 7.5 (7.5.5 Licensing Transactions, 7.5.6 royalty-stream sales, 7.5.7 further negative pledges) are financing/collateral-protection covenants tied to the funded Product, not non-compete or field-of-use restraints: 7.5.5 leaves PB free to enter any Excluded Licensing Transaction (expressly including licensing its ELP technology products such as PB1046 and PB1023) without SFJ consent, and consent elsewhere may only be withheld on a reasoned \"Material Impact\" determination subject to expedited arbitration. This meets the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-16a798a0","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"PB has no usable convenience exit. 14.2.2 is gated on SFJ having paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs, closes on receipt of the first Regulatory Approval, carries a redacted notice period, and conditions the exit on paying SFJ 300% of Development Costs, so over a Term running to the last Approval Payment (14.1) PB cannot leave on notice at the preferred (30 days) or fallback (60-90 days) standard. That fails the fallback on material terms. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Co-Development Agreement (Execution Version)

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel (for PB / Customer)
**Re:** Playbook review of the SFJ Co-Development Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Execution Version against our playbook. Nine of the eighteen rules are met, several of them comfortably in our favour: PB carries no exclusivity, non-compete or MFN obligation, SFJ has no audit right over PB, there is no auto-renewal or renewal uplift, and PB owns Trial Inventions outright with freely-assignable, multi-tier sublicensable flow-down licences (licence scope sits at or above the fallback).

The problems cluster in three places. First, **ownership of our own data**: Section 11.1.1.4 vests the Trial Data Package — all clinical trial data and Research Results generated under our Development Program — in SFJ until we buy it back. Second, **IP indemnity asymmetry**: SFJ's indemnity says nothing about third-party IP infringement, while PB's indemnity at 12.1.2(f) covers infringement caused by "either Party", so PB carries a one-way IP indemnity that also protects SFJ for SFJ's own conduct. Third, **the exit economics**: Article 14.2 imposes formula-driven termination payments on PB of 100%–300% of Development Costs (plus a 25% interest variant), PB has no workable convenience exit, SFJ may terminate on a Change of Control of PB, and Section 4.2.3(ii) locks us into a $110 million minimum funding election.

Supporting gaps: no liability cap at all (both sides uncapped, no carve-outs), arbitration rather than the Delaware courts that match the Delaware governing law, no SFJ performance warranty (Section 13.6.2 disclaims everything outside Article 13), no general post-exit transition or data-export right, an over-long non-solicit tail, and no SFJ-level E&O or cyber cover.

One item requires attention before we send: the termination-for-convenience redline is marked **needs_review** and failed verification. It should not go out in its current form.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Adding a reciprocal SFJ IP indemnity with standard exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x-annual-amounts super-cap (non-zero floor); narrowing 12.1.2(f) to PB's own performance. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | Intellectual Property and PII (§ 11.1.1.4) | SFJ is sole owner of the Trial Data Package until PB buys it back. Flipping ownership to PB, limiting SFJ to processing to perform its obligations, conforming the Exhibit K mechanic; payment consideration and the 14.3.1 backstop assignment left intact. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.2.6; § 15.6 | SFJ may terminate on a PB Change of Control (150% of Development Costs); no-consent carve-out is mutual; competitor bar lapses at Program Transfer. Targeting preferred: PB-only carve-out, reasonableness standard for SFJ, permanent competitor bar, removal of 14.2.6 and its dependent consequences. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | Term and Termination (§§ 14.2.1–14.2.10) | Termination payments of 300% / 150% / 100% of Development Costs, plus Development Costs at 25% annual interest. | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | Intellectual Property and PII (§§ 11.1.1.3–11.1.1.4) | Sits at or above the fallback: PB owns Trial Inventions and the flow-down licences are worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable and sublicensable through multiple tiers. | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | Development Costs (§ 4.2.3(ii)) | $110m minimum Elected Total Amount with no reduction mechanic and no true-up exit. Deleting the floor only; the $120m ceiling, election mechanic, overrun allocation and use-of-funds covenant untouched, as § 6.2 already pro-rates our Approval Payments. |

| Medium | TRANSITION | Missing | Term and Termination (§ 14.3; cf. § 10.3) | § 14.3 is conditional on a § 14.2 termination and no Program Transfer, so it does not apply on expiration; § 10.3 has no export deadline. | Medium | WARRANTY | Missing | Representations and Warranties (§ 13.5; § 13.6.2) | SFJ's performance is effectively "AS IS"; § 13.6.2 disclaims all warranties outside Article 13. | Medium | AUDIT | Compliant | Records (Art. 9; §§ 3.6, 3.18.2) | Better than preferred: SFJ has no audit or inspection right over PB. § 3.6 obligations are mutual or PB-controlled; § 3.18.2 is a reporting covenant. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | Security Interest (§ 7.5) | Meets preferred: no MFN, ROFR or matching obligation on PB. The "not less favorable" language is a lender subordination benchmark. |
| Medium | RENEWAL | Compliant | Term and Termination (§ 14.1) | Meets preferred: finite Term ending on the last Approval Payment, no evergreen or renewal uplift. Absence of an express "renewal by mutual written agreement" statement is a wording point only. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | Indemnification and Insurance (§ 12.3) | Mutual programme in place, but E&O binds only professional-services subcontractors and there is no cyber/privacy cover; stated limits are redacted. Adding SFJ-level E&O of USD 1m and cyber/privacy of USD 2m in § 12.3.2, leaving the mutual structure and other limits untouched. |

---

## Walk-away items

These three sit at or across our walk-away line and should be treated as conditions of signing rather than negotiable trades:

1. **SFJ ownership of the Trial Data Package (§ 11.1.1.4).** Vesting the data and Research Results generated under our own Development Program in the counterparty, recoverable only by buy-back, is walk-away territory and gives SFJ rights far beyond processing to perform the services.
2. **The one-way IP indemnity (Art. 12).** No SFJ IP indemnity at all, combined with PB indemnifying infringement caused by "either Party", fails the fallback and sits at the walk-away line.
3. **SFJ's Change of Control termination right (§ 14.2.6).** A counterparty right to terminate in its sole discretion on a Change of Control of PB, with a 150% Development Costs payment, is expressly walk-away territory.

We would also treat the breach-triggered 300% Development Cost multiples under LD as close to that line; they fail both the preferred and fallback positions and are punitive in character.

---

## Next steps

1. **Hold the T4C redline.** The termination-for-convenience proposal failed verification and is flagged needs_review. We will re-draft against § 14.2.2 (including the orphaned credit cross-reference and the § 5.2.2.2 reference to § 14.2.10) and re-verify before it leaves our side.
2. **Confirm commercial mandate on the three walk-away items** with the business team, so we can state clearly in the cover note that data ownership, the reciprocal IP indemnity and deletion of § 14.2.6 are not trades.
3. **Ask for the redacted figures** we cannot price: the § 12.3 insurance limits, the § 14.2.2 notice period, the § 14.3.4(ii) trial-transfer period and the § 15.16 non-solicit tail. Several of our positions are calibrated to the fallback only because the numbers are unavailable.
4. **Circulate the verified redline** covering INDEMN, IP, ASSIGN, LD, GOVLAW, LOL-CAP, MINCOMMIT, NOSOLICIT, TRANSITION, WARRANTY and INSURANCE, noting in the cover note that we are not marking up the nine compliant rules.
5. **Flag the preferred-level upgrades we did not press**, for use as give-and-take in negotiation: the USD 1m liability floor and data-protection/fraud/IP carve-outs under LOL-CAP; "perpetual/irrevocable" licence labelling; then-current rates, machine-readable format and deletion certification under TRANSITION; and the 12-month, workmanlike-standard warranty."}

## Walk-away items

These three sit at or across our walk-away line and should be treated as conditions of signing rather than negotiable trades:

1. **SFJ ownership of the Trial Data Package (§ 11.1.1.4).** Vesting the data and Research Results generated under our own Development Program in the counterparty, recoverable only by buy-back, is walk-away territory and gives SFJ rights far beyond processing to perform the services.
2. **The one-way IP indemnity (Art. 12).** No SFJ IP indemnity at all, combined with PB indemnifying infringement caused by "either Party", fails the fallback and sits at the walk-away line.
3. **SFJ's Change of Control termination right (§ 14.2.6).** A counterparty right to terminate in its sole discretion on a Change of Control of PB, with a 150% Development Costs payment, is expressly walk-away territory.

We would also treat the breach-triggered 300% Development Cost multiples under LD as close to that line; they fail both the preferred and fallback positions and are punitive in character.
